message.content: Trade strengthened pharaohs' powers because it brought them wealth, prestige, and control. They used their profits to feed their people, reward their officials, and equip their armies. He, the pharaoh, was seen by them as the source of their prosperity, and they reinforced his authority with their taxes, their rituals, and their labor. His power grew when their routes were safe, but it could shrink if their caravans failed. We should note that their dependence on trade made their rule both flexible and fragile; if their merchants prospered, their loyalty was easier to maintain, and if their shipments stopped, their people might question their leaders, challenge their legitimacy, or turn to their rivals. Their success, therefore, helped them secure their position, and their failures showed that their power always relied on their ability to manage their resources, their allies, and their people.
